discovery: Experimental demonstration of fractionally charged quasiparticles and anyonic quantum statistics in the fractional quantum Hall effect

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'Ecole Normale Supérieure (ENS-PSL, CNRS), Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics (fractional quantum Hall effect, anyons, topological order)
motivation: Anyons, particles that are neither bosons nor fermions, were a theoretical idea for decades. These nominees turned them into measured reality. Heiblum's shot-noise experiments directly measured fractional charges (e/3, then e/4 at filling 5/2, and more) of quasiparticles in the fractional quantum Hall effect, and his group later probed neutral modes and thermal Hall conductance. Fève's anyon-collider experiments (2020) showed fractional exchange statistics through two-particle correlations. Manfra built ultra-high-mobility heterostructures and Fabry-Perot interferometers that showed anyonic braiding phases directly (2020), which opened a path to non-Abelian interferometry. Together these experiments showed that emergent quasiparticles in two-dimensional electron systems carry fractional charge and fractional statistics. This is a basic new fact about quantum matter. It underlies topological quantum computation and the current search for anyons in moiré and graphene systems.
